title: Plans and the future
goal: Talk about plans and what's going to happen — in three subtly different ways, without falling for the idea that *vil* means "will".
bekal: use *ætla að*, *munu*, and the present tense to talk about the future

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Hringurinn í sumar
dialogs.intro: May, and the sun is starting to refuse to set. Búdí is planning his first trip around the island.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Hvað ætlarðu að gera í sumar?
lines.id: What are you going to do this summer?
lines.literal: what intend-you to do in summer?

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.id: I'm going to travel around the island.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Allan hringveginn? Það tekur að minnsta kosti viku.
lines.id: The whole Ring Road? That takes at least a week.
lines.literal: whole ring-road-the? it takes at least week.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Ég veit. Ég tek tíu daga í frí.
lines.id: I know. I'm taking ten days off.
lines.literal: I know. I take ten days in vacation.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Nei, Sigga kemur með. Við leigjum bíl.
lines.id: No, Sigga's coming along. We're renting a car.
lines.literal: no, Sigga comes with. we rent car.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Farið varlega. Vegirnir verða þröngir fyrir austan.
lines.id: Be careful. The roads get narrow in the east.
lines.literal: go carefully. roads-the become narrow to-the east.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Við munum keyra hægt, ég lofa.
lines.literal: we will drive slowly, I promise.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Og ef veðrið versnar, þá stoppið þið.
lines.id: And if the weather gets worse, you stop.
lines.literal: and if weather-the worsens, then stop you.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Já. Ég veit að veðrið breytist fljótt hér.
lines.id: Yes. I know the weather changes fast here.
lines.literal: yes. I know that weather-the changes fast here.

lines.speaker: Anna:
lines.text: Gott. Þegar þú kemur til baka, viltu segja mér allt.
lines.id: Good. When you get back, you have to tell me everything.
lines.literal: good. when you come back, want-you tell me all.

lines.speaker: Búdí:
lines.text: Að sjálfsögðu. Ég sendi þér myndir á hverjum degi!
lines.id: Of course. I'll send you pictures every day!
lines.literal: of-course self-said. I send you pictures on every day!

notes: **Icelandic has no future verb form.** *Ég sendi þér myndir* can mean "I send" or "I'll send"; the time expression decides. English does this too: "I'm leaving tomorrow" is present in form, future in meaning.

**Ætla að is the most common way, and it expresses INTENTION.** *Ég ætla að ferðast* = I'm going to travel. When you're talking about your own plans, this is almost always the right form — think "going to".

⚠️ **Vil means "want", not "will".** *Ég vil fara* = I **want** to go. "I will go" is *ég ætla að fara* or *ég fer*. English speakers make this mistake constantly because the words look alike, and the meaning shifts a long way — from plan to wish.

**Munu is used for predictions and formal statements**, not personal plans. *Það mun rigna á morgun* — it will rain tomorrow. In everyday conversation it sounds a bit distant; in the news and in writing, it's everywhere.

**Icelandic clauses do NOT change their word order** — and that's big good news. *Ég veit að veðrið breytist* — exactly the same order as a standalone sentence. Norwegian, Danish, and German all move something in a clause; Icelandic doesn't.

**But if the clause comes FIRST, the verb-second rule still applies**: *Ef veðrið versnar, **þá stoppið þið***. The whole clause counts as one element in first place, so the main verb jumps ahead of its subject.

grammars.title: Three ways to talk about the future
body: All three are correct; what differs is the tone and how certain it is.

head: Form
Example
English
Used for
rows: things that are certain, with a time expression

after: The six forms of *munu*: *ég mun, þú munt, hann mun, við munum, þið munuð, þeir munu*. It's followed by a verb **without** *að*.
If you're in doubt, use *ætla að*. It's almost never wrong for people's plans, and that's what you'll talk about most.

grammars.title: Clauses
body: The three most common linking words, and one piece of good news: the word order stays normal.

head: Conjunction
English
Example
Meaning
rows: If it rains, we're not going.
When I get home, I eat.
*Ég fer af því að ég vil sjá það.*
I'm going because I want to see it.

after: ***Ekki* stays where it is**: *Ég veit að hann kemur **ekki***. Compare Norwegian, which moves it in front of the verb in a clause — Icelandic doesn't, so you have one rule less to learn.

When the clause comes first, *þá* is often added as a marker: *Ef veðrið versnar, **þá** stoppið þið.* That *þá* isn't required, but you'll hear it a lot, and it makes the sentence easier to follow — like English "if …, then …".

blocks.text: *Ég hlakka til* is literally "I laugh toward", and it means "I'm looking forward to it". It's one of the most used Icelandic expressions and one of the hardest to translate — use it as it is.

sections.title: Hringvegurinn: one road around the country

blocks.text: *Þjóðvegur 1*, which everyone calls *hringvegurinn*, is a **1,332-kilometer** road that circles the whole island. It was only finished in 1974, when the last bridge over the glacial rivers in the south was finally built. Before that, there was no way to drive around Iceland at all.

blocks.title: Three things you must know before driving in Iceland
items: **The weather changes within minutes.** Icelanders check *vedur.is* for weather and *road.is* for road conditions every morning, not just now and then.
**Single-lane bridges everywhere.** Whoever gets there first goes first. Stop and wait — overtaking on one of those bridges is the fastest way to end up in the news.
**Off-road driving is strictly forbidden.** Icelandic moss takes decades to recover from a single tire track, and the fines are huge. *Utanvegaakstur bannaður* — the signs are everywhere.

exercises.prompt: Choose the right form for the meaning.
items: I'm going to go tomorrow: Ég ____ (vil, ætla að) fara á morgun.
I want coffee: Ég ____ (vil, ætla að) kaffi.
It will rain tomorrow: Það ____ (mun, vill) rigna á morgun.
We're going to rent a car: Við ____ (viljum, ætlum að) leigja bíl.
She wants to go home now: Hún ____ (vill, mun) fara heim núna.
